summary: This note describes the 2016 NBA draft, held June 23, 2016 at Barclays Center in Brooklyn and televised nationally by ESPN. It notes that The Vertical live streamed the draft for the first time in NBA draft history. It also explains the May 17, 2016 draft lottery, in which non-playoff teams kept their designated positions for the first time since the lottery was introduced in 1985, giving the Philadelphia 76ers the No. 1 pick, the Los Angeles Lakers No. 2, and the Boston Celtics (via the Brooklyn Nets) No. 3.
one_line: Overview of the June 23, 2016 NBA draft at Barclays Center, including its ESPN broadcast and the May 2016 lottery results.
key_facts: The 2016 NBA draft was held on June 23, 2016, at Barclays Center in Brooklyn.
The draft was televised nationally in the U.S. by ESPN.
The Vertical live streamed the NBA draft for the first time in NBA draft history.
NBA teams took turns selecting amateur U.S. college basketball players and other eligible players, including international players.
The draft lottery took place during the playoffs, on May 17, 2016.
This was the first time since the lottery system was introduced in 1985 that all non-playoff teams remained in their exact designated spots.
The Philadelphia 76ers, with a 10-72 record, received the No. 1 pick in the 2016 draft.
The Los Angeles Lakers kept the No. 2 pick in the 2016 draft.
The Boston Celtics, via the Brooklyn Nets, got the No. 3 pick in the 2016 draft.
Non-playoff teams' draft positions were based on regular season standings from the 2015-16 season.
